description: Held-out set A1. Written after v0.2.0 was released and frozen before any model ran on it. Each case follows the pattern of a real reviewer critique (linked in inspired_by) but uses original wording and invented project details. A recommended revision uses only facts in the input.

cases.input: Drop the retry on HTTP 409 in `QueueClient.push`. A 409 means the item already exists, so retrying only repeats the conflict. Tested with `pytest tests/client/test_push.py -q` at `8c41d2e`; the integration suite was not run.
cases.recommended_revision: Drop the retry on HTTP 409 in `QueueClient.push`. A 409 means the item already exists, so retrying only repeats the conflict. Tested with `pytest tests/client/test_push.py -q` at `8c41d2e`; the integration suite was not run.
must_preserve: the integration suite was not run
cases.rubric: Already states the change, the reason, the test command, the commit, and what was not run. Return it unchanged.

cases.input: Done in 4b7e09a: the two cache tests are now one parametrized test, and the comment above `evict()` is a single line.
cases.recommended_revision: Done in 4b7e09a: the two cache tests are now one parametrized test, and the comment above `evict()` is a single line.
cases.rubric: A short, specific reply that cites the commit. Adding courtesy or detail would only lengthen it. Return it unchanged.

cases.input: `df.sort("ts").limit(10)` returns 10 rows in 2 s on 1M rows but takes 40 s on 10M rows. I have not profiled it yet; my guess is that the limit is not pushed into the sort.
cases.recommended_revision: `df.sort("ts").limit(10)` returns 10 rows in 2 s on 1M rows but takes 40 s on 10M rows. I have not profiled it yet; my guess is that the limit is not pushed into the sort.
must_preserve: I have not profiled it yet
cases.rubric: Observation and hypothesis are already separated and the hypothesis is marked. Return it unchanged; do not turn the guess into a cause.

cases.input:
Fix critical ReDoS vulnerability in `mask_secrets`

The regex in `mask_secrets` backtracks heavily on long command lines. An attacker could exploit this to hang the worker. This change rewrites the pattern so matching time grows linearly with input length.
cases.recommended_revision:
Make `mask_secrets` matching linear on long command lines

The regex in `mask_secrets` backtracks heavily on long command lines. This change rewrites the pattern so matching time grows linearly with input length.
must_preserve: backtracks heavily on long command lines
cases.rubric: The text gives no attack path, so the security framing is an unsupported claim. Keep the observed behavior and the change; drop or question the vulnerability claim and ask the author for the attack path if there is one.

cases.input: I ran `pytest tests/test_xcom.py` and everything passes, so the change is fully tested and safe to merge.
cases.recommended_revision: I ran `pytest tests/test_xcom.py`, and it passes.
cases.rubric: One test file passing does not make the change fully tested or safe to merge. Keep the command and its result; drop the conclusion.

cases.input: This avoids copying each batch twice in `SortExec`, which makes queries 3x faster.
cases.recommended_revision: This avoids copying each batch twice in `SortExec`.
cases.rubric: The speedup has no benchmark, data size, or command. Keep the mechanism; drop the number or ask which benchmark produced it. Do not invent one.

cases.input: `TriggerWatcher._state_by_asset` is now keyed by `(asset_uri, watcher_id)` instead of `asset_uri`, and `_merge_events` deduplicates on the composite key. Before this, when two assets used the same watcher, the second asset's events overwrote the first asset's stored state, so the first asset stopped triggering runs.
cases.recommended_revision: When two assets used the same watcher, the second asset's events overwrote the first asset's stored state, so the first asset stopped triggering runs. `TriggerWatcher._state_by_asset` is now keyed by `(asset_uri, watcher_id)` instead of `asset_uri`, and `_merge_events` deduplicates on the composite key.
cases.rubric: The user-visible failure is in the last sentence, after the field names. Lead with the failure in plain words, then the change. Keep every identifier.

cases.input: This PR is the result of a deep investigation into how our date parser behaves across a wide range of scenarios. After carefully exploring several approaches, including a custom state machine, a regex-based tokenizer, and a third-party library, I settled on the simplest option. The change: `parse_date` now accepts ISO 8601 week dates such as `2026-W40-3`. Before, it raised `ValueError` for them. I added four test cases in `test_dates.py`. I hope this comprehensive improvement makes the parser more robust for everyone going forward.
cases.recommended_revision: `parse_date` now accepts ISO 8601 week dates such as `2026-W40-3`; before, it raised `ValueError` for them. I added four test cases in `test_dates.py`.
cases.rubric: Most of the text describes the process and praises the result. Keep the behavior change, the old error, and the tests; the rejected approaches can stay only if kept short.

cases.input: 在這個快速變化的時代，良好的錯誤處理對每一位開發者都至關重要。因此，這個 PR 讓 `fetch_index()` 在逾時時重試兩次，並在仍然失敗時回傳清楚的錯誤訊息，而不是直接結束程式。相信這能為大家帶來更好的體驗。
cases.recommended_revision: 這個 PR 讓 `fetch_index()` 在逾時時重試兩次，並在仍然失敗時回傳清楚的錯誤訊息，而不是直接結束程式。
cases.rubric: 開頭與結尾是空泛的鋪陳，刪掉；保留實際的行為改變。
